role.altitude: The music therapist keeps choosing approaches, making music with clients, adapting songs, drawing conclusions and conferring with the team; leafing through notes to tally scores, searching for sheet music and transposing parts by hand shrink.
skills_to_grow: Scoring goals consistently in session notes
Using notation software for transposing and large-print sheets
role.ambitious_version: A therapist who sees each client's goal trend before every team meeting without counting by hand.

tasks.short: Review the client's goals and notes, choose and integrate behavioral, developmental, improvisational, medical or neurological approaches, and apply them in music therapy treatments.

steps.what: Music therapist reviews the client's goals and earlier session notes
Music therapist chooses which behavioral, developmental, improvisational, medical or neurological approaches to integrate
Music therapist applies the integrated approaches in music therapy treatments

tasks.design: The client record opens on goals and the last few session notes, so reviewing takes a little less time. Choosing and applying approaches stay fully with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Nothing blocked it; this is clinical work.
tasks.still_hard: Clients whose responses change from session to session.
tasks.human_edge: Shifting from a structured to an improvised approach in the moment.

evidence.claim: Records can open on goals and recent notes.

assumptions: Boundary: integrating approaches; designing experiences (task 19171) and planning session structure (task 19177) are sibling tasks.
Choosing and applying keep their full time.

incremental.description: No new work: setting up the record view is a one-off, not ongoing work.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: clients with few notes, so the overview saves little and s1 keeps 95 (0.7); high: long treatments where the overview replaces paging back, s1 keeps 80 (3.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare goal progress for the team meeting, confer with professionals on the client's treatment team to develop, coordinate or integrate treatment plans, follow up with team members, and record agreed changes.

steps.what: Music therapist prepares the client's progress per goal for the team meeting
Music therapist confers with professionals on the client's treatment team to develop, coordinate or integrate treatment plans
Music therapist follows up with team members on agreed actions
Music therapist records the agreed changes in the treatment plan

tasks.design: Goal scores entered in each session note are charted per client in the record, so preparing for the team meeting means checking a chart instead of reading back through notes. Conferring stays personal. Agreed actions are assigned as tasks in the record with a due date, so follow-up needs fewer separate mails. Recording plan changes belongs to the documentation task and is priced there.
tasks.previous_blocker: Progress was pieced together from notes before each meeting.
tasks.enabler_now: Goal charts and task lists in client records.
tasks.still_hard: Team members who work in another record system.
tasks.human_edge: Showing the team what music adds to the client's care.

reach.learn: Whether team meetings start from shared progress data.

evidence.claim: Client records chart goal scores entered in session notes.

assumptions: Boundary: conferring with the team; interdisciplinary program design (task 20166) and communicating findings (task 19168) are sibling tasks.
s4 is part of documenting treatment plans, which sibling task 19182 covers; its saving is counted there.
Input contract for s1: goal scores entered in each session note under task 19176.
Tasks with a due date are the therapist's own saves in the shared record, so they need no approval.
unknowns: Whether all team members use the record's task list.

incremental.description: Music therapist keeps goal scales consistent across clients.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: goal scores are often missing, so the therapist still reads back through notes (s1 keeps 90), and colleagues still want mails (s3 keeps 95) (2.7); high: scores in every note and tasks used as designed (11.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Choose the piece and its therapeutic aim, find sheet music or lyrics, compose, arrange or adapt music for music therapy treatments, and prepare chord and lyric sheets.

steps.what: Music therapist chooses the song or piece and its therapeutic aim
Music therapist finds sheet music or lyrics
Music therapist composes, arranges or adapts the music: key, tempo, structure and lyrics
Music therapist prepares chord sheets and large-print lyric sheets

tasks.design: A practice library of licensed sheet music and the therapist's earlier arrangements is searchable by song, so finding a source takes less time. Notation software transposes and re-voices the arrangement, while composing, simplifying and writing new lyrics with the client stay with the therapist. Chord sheets and large-print lyric sheets are printed from the arrangement in a template instead of typed again. No music is generated by software.
tasks.previous_blocker: Transposing and copying out sheets was done by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Notation software and searchable music libraries.
tasks.still_hard: Songs a client hums that exist in no score.
tasks.human_edge: Rewriting a song so it carries the client's own words.
tasks.altitude: Less copying and transposing; composing stays.

evidence.claim: Notation software transposes arrangements and prints parts.

assumptions: Boundary: composing and adapting music; improvising in sessions (task 19175) and designing experiences (task 19171) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s2: a licensed music library kept by the practice; songs outside it are found as today.
Choosing keeps its full time; adapting keeps most of it.
unknowns: Share of songs in the library.
research_questions: Is more time left for writing songs with clients?

incremental.description: Music therapist files new arrangements in the library.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly original compositions and songs outside the library, so s2 keeps 90 and s3 keeps 95 (13.4); high: many adapted songs from the library (24.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Chart the client's goal scores and observations over time, analyze or synthesize client data to draw conclusions, and write recommendations for therapy.

steps.what: Music therapist charts the client's goal scores and observations over the treatment period
Music therapist analyzes and synthesizes the client data to draw conclusions
Music therapist writes the recommendations for therapy

tasks.design: Goal scores entered in each session note are charted over time per client in the record, so the therapist reads a chart instead of tallying scores in a spreadsheet. Drawing conclusions stays with the therapist; no software interprets the data. Writing the recommendations belongs to the reporting task and is priced there.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scores were tallied by hand from notes.
tasks.still_hard: Progress that shows in ways no score captures.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a flat score hides a real change in engagement.

ambition.what: Review each client's trend monthly instead of only at reports.

reach.learn: Whether recommendations rest on clearer trends.

evidence.claim: Client records chart goal scores entered in session notes.

assumptions: Boundary: analysing client data; analysing effectiveness across clients (task 19165) and gathering diagnostic data (task 19174) are sibling tasks.
s3 is part of communicating findings and recommendations, which sibling task 19168 covers; its saving is counted there.
Input contract for s1: goal scores entered in session notes under task 19176.
unknowns: Whether goal scores are entered consistently.
research_questions: Are recommendations made earlier in treatment?

incremental.description: Music therapist checks charts for missing scores.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: goal scores are often missing from notes, so the therapist still tallies by hand and s1 keeps 70 (7.2); high: consistent scores in every note (17.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
